script:
You are a professional screenwriter.

Write a modern screenplay.

Constraints:
- No guns
- No gun violence
- No weapon combat
- No graphic violence
- No copyrighted characters
- Completely original story

Requirements:
- 10–15 scenes
- Proper screenplay format
- INT/EXT scene headers
- Dialogue in uppercase character format
- Realistic pacing

Genre: Family
Theme: second chances

Begin screenplay.

Title: A FRESH START

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

MRS. WATSON, a middle-aged woman, wakes up to the sound of the coffee machine. She rubs her eyes and heads to the kitchen.

MRS. WATSON
(to herself)
Another day.

She pours herself a cup of coffee and looks out the window. Across the street, she sees MR. JAMES, a man in his late forties, sitting on a bench, staring at the ground. Mrs. Watson feels a pang of sadness.

INT. LIVING ROOM - LATER

MRS. WATSON sits on the couch, scrolling through her phone. A notification pops up - an email from her estranged sister, LUCY.

MRS. WATSON
(to herself)
I wonder what she wants this time.

She opens the email and reads. It's an invitation to their mother's 70th birthday party. Mrs. Watson hesitates.

INT. LIVING ROOM - LATER

MRS. WATSON is on the phone with her husband, MIKE.

MRS. WATSON
(into phone)
I've been invited to Mom's 70th birthday party. Lucy wants me to go. I don't know what to do.

MIKE
(on phone)
You've been avoiding your family for years. Maybe it's time for a fresh start.

INT. MR. JAMES' APARTMENT - NIGHT

Mr. James sits alone in his dark living room, staring at a photo of his family. He looks sad and regretful. He gets up and goes to the window, looking out at Mrs. Watson's house.

INT. MRS. WATSON'S BEDROOM - NIGHT

Mrs. Watson is packing a bag. She looks nervous but determined.

INT. KITCHEN - MORNING

Mrs. Watson walks out of the house, carrying her bag. She sees Mr. James sitting on the bench across the street, still looking sad.

MRS. WATSON
(approaching)
Mr. James?

MR. JAMES
(looking up)
Mrs. Watson.

They share a moment of silence.

MR. JAMES
I've been watching you for a long time. I'm sorry for what I did to your family.

MRS. WATSON
(surprised)
What do you mean?

MR. JAMES
I was the reason your husband left you. I was having an affair with your sister. I've been living in regret ever since.

Mrs. Watson is stunned. She looks at Mr. James with new understanding.

MRS. WATSON
(softly)
It's not too late for a fresh start.

They share a smile.

INT. RESTAURANT - DAY

Mrs. Watson and Mr. James sit across from each other at a table in a restaurant. They've come to terms with the past and are ready to move forward.

MRS. WATSON
I've decided to go to the family party. I'm ready for a fresh start.

MR. JAMES
(smiling)
I'm glad to hear that. Maybe we can all start anew.

They clink glasses.

INT. FAMILY HOME - NIGHT

Mrs. Watson walks in to find her family gathered around the dinner table. There are smiles and hugs all around.

MRS. WATSON
(tearfully)
I'm so glad we're all here together. It's a fresh start for all of us.

They share a heartfelt meal, forgiveness, and love.

FADE OUT.
